name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MATCHING_Q01 - Isotopes of hydrogen and properties

questiontext.text:
Match the hydrogen species in List I with their correct characteristic in List II:

List IList II
(A) Protium (\({}^{1}\mathrm{H}\))(i) Radioactive \(\beta\)-emitter with \(t_{1/2} = 12.33\text{ years}\)
(B) Deuterium (\({}^{2}\mathrm{H}\))(ii) Predominant form of terrestrial deuterium
(C) Tritium (\({}^{3}\mathrm{H}\))(iii) Contains zero neutrons in the nucleus
(D) \(\mathrm{HD}\)(iv) Contains one neutron in the nucleus

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The three isotopes of hydrogen have atomic number \(1\) (one proton) and differ in the number of neutrons in their nuclei.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
- Protium (\({}^{1}\mathrm{H}\)) has mass number \(1\), so it contains \(1 - 1 = 0\) neutrons in its nucleus.
- Deuterium (\({}^{2}\mathrm{H}\) or \(\mathrm{D}\)) has mass number \(2\), so it contains \(2 - 1 = 1\) neutron in its nucleus.
- Tritium (\({}^{3}\mathrm{H}\) or \(\mathrm{T}\)) has mass number \(3\) (\(2\) neutrons) and is the only radioactive isotope of hydrogen, emitting low-energy \(\beta\) particles with a half-life of \(12.33\text{ years}\).
- Terrestrial hydrogen contains \(0.0156\%\) deuterium, which exists predominantly in the form of \(\mathrm{HD}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, protium corresponds to zero neutrons, deuterium corresponds to one neutron, tritium corresponds to the radioactive isotope with \(t_{1/2} = 12.33\text{ years}\), and \(\mathrm{HD}\) corresponds to the predominant terrestrial form of deuterium.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MATCHING_Q02 - Classification of hydrides and examples

questiontext.text:
Match the hydride category in List I with a suitable example in List II:

List IList II
(A) Ionic (saline) hydride(i) \(\mathrm{CH}_4\)
(B) Electron-deficient molecular hydride(ii) \(\mathrm{NaH}\)
(C) Electron-precise molecular hydride(iii) \(\mathrm{NH}_3\)
(D) Electron-rich molecular hydride(iv) \(\mathrm{B}_2\mathrm{H}_6\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hydrides are classified as ionic (saline) hydrides formed by highly electropositive \(s\)-block elements, or covalent (molecular) hydrides formed by \(p\)-block elements, which are further divided into electron-deficient, electron-precise, and electron-rich based on their valence electron count.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
- \(\mathrm{NaH}\) is a stoichiometric ionic (saline) hydride formed by the alkali metal sodium.
- \(\mathrm{B}_2\mathrm{H}_6\) (diborane) is formed by a group 13 element and has too few electrons for a conventional Lewis structure, making it an electron-deficient molecular hydride.
- \(\mathrm{CH}_4\) (methane) is formed by a group 14 element and has the exact number of electrons required for a conventional Lewis structure, making it an electron-precise molecular hydride.
- \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) (ammonia) is formed by a group 15 element and has excess electrons present as a lone pair, making it an electron-rich molecular hydride.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Matching each category with its example gives: ionic hydride \(\rightarrow \mathrm{NaH}\), electron-deficient \(\rightarrow \mathrm{B}_2\mathrm{H}_6\), electron-precise \(\rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_4\), and electron-rich \(\rightarrow \mathrm{NH}_3\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MATCHING_Q03 - Types of water and their causes

questiontext.text:
Match the type of water in List I with its correct description or cause in List II:

List IList II
(A) Soft water(i) Caused by soluble chlorides and sulphates of \(\mathrm{Ca}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg}\)
(B) Temporary hard water(ii) \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\), used as a moderator in nuclear reactors
(C) Permanent hard water(iii) Free from soluble salts of \(\mathrm{Ca}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg}\); gives lather easily
(D) Heavy water(iv) Caused by soluble hydrogencarbonates of \(\mathrm{Ca}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Water quality with respect to soap lathering depends on dissolved \(\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}\) salts, while isotopic substitution of hydrogen by deuterium gives heavy water.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
- Soft water is free from soluble salts of calcium and magnesium and gives lather with soap easily.
- Temporary hardness is due to the presence of magnesium and calcium hydrogencarbonates.
- Permanent hardness is due to the presence of soluble chlorides and sulphates of magnesium and calcium.
- Heavy water (\(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\)) is extensively used as a moderator in nuclear reactors.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, soft water pairs with freedom from soluble \(\mathrm{Ca}/\mathrm{Mg}\) salts, temporary hard water with hydrogencarbonates, permanent hard water with chlorides and sulphates, and heavy water with \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MATCHING_Q04 - Industrial processes and chemical reactions

questiontext.text:
Match the industrial term or process in List I with its corresponding chemical representation in List II:

List IList II
(A) Syngas(i) \(\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g}) \xrightarrow{673\text{ K}} \mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g})\)
(B) Coal gasification(ii) \(3\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Fe},\, 673\text{ K}} 2\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g})\)
(C) Water-gas shift reaction(iii) Mixture of \(\mathrm{CO}\) and \(\mathrm{H}_2\)
(D) Haber process(iv) \(\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g}) \xrightarrow{1270\text{ K}} \mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g})\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Commercial dihydrogen production from coal and hydrocarbons involves synthesis gas formation and the water-gas shift reaction, while a major industrial use of dihydrogen is ammonia synthesis via the Haber process.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
- Syngas (synthesis gas or water gas) is a mixture of \(\mathrm{CO}\) and \(\mathrm{H}_2\).
- Coal gasification is the process of producing syngas by reacting coke/coal with steam at \(1270\text{ K}\): \(\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g}) \xrightarrow{1270\text{ K}} \mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g})\).
- The water-gas shift reaction increases \(\mathrm{H}_2\) yield by reacting \(\mathrm{CO}\) of syngas with steam at \(673\text{ K}\) in the presence of an iron chromate catalyst to form \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) and \(\mathrm{H}_2\).
- The Haber process manufactures ammonia from \(\mathrm{N}_2\) and \(\mathrm{H}_2\) at \(673\text{ K}\) and \(200\text{ atm}\) over an iron catalyst.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, syngas pairs with the \(\mathrm{CO} + \mathrm{H}_2\) mixture, coal gasification with \(\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), water-gas shift reaction with \(\mathrm{CO} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), and Haber process with \(\mathrm{N}_2 + 3\mathrm{H}_2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MATCHING_Q05 - Water softening methods and reagents

questiontext.text:
Match the water-softening method in List I with the reagent or material used in List II:

List IList II
(A) Clark's method(i) Sodium hexametaphosphate (\(\mathrm{Na_6P_6O_{18}}\))
(B) Calgon's method(ii) Hydrated sodium aluminium silicate (\(\mathrm{NaAlSiO_4}\))
(C) Permutit process(iii) Calculated amount of lime (\(\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}\))
(D) Washing soda treatment(iv) Sodium carbonate (\(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Temporary hardness is removed by Clark's method, whereas permanent hardness is removed by washing soda treatment, Calgon's method, or the permutit (zeolite) ion-exchange process.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
- Clark's method adds a calculated amount of lime, \(\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}\), to precipitate \(\mathrm{CaCO_3}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg(OH)_2}\).
- Calgon's method uses sodium hexametaphosphate (\(\mathrm{Na_6P_6O_{18}}\)) to sequester \(\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}\) as soluble complex anions.
- The permutit or zeolite process uses hydrated sodium aluminium silicate (\(\mathrm{NaAlSiO_4}\)) to exchange \(\mathrm{Na^+}\) ions for \(\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}\).
- Washing soda treatment uses sodium carbonate (\(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}\)) to precipitate insoluble \(\mathrm{CaCO_3}\) and \(\mathrm{MgCO_3}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, Clark's method pairs with \(\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}\), Calgon's method with \(\mathrm{Na_6P_6O_{18}}\), the permutit process with \(\mathrm{NaAlSiO_4}\), and washing soda treatment with \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MATCHING_Q06 - Types of hydrates and examples

questiontext.text:
Match the hydrated species in List I with the type of water association in List II:

List IList II
(A) \([\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]^{3+} 3\mathrm{Cl}^-\)(i) Interstitial water
(B) \(\mathrm{BaCl}_2 \cdot 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)(ii) Hydrogen-bonded water
(C) Water outside coordination sphere in \([\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_4]^{2+}\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}\cdot \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)(iii) Coordinated water
(D) \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2 \cdot \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)(iv) Hydrate of hydrogen peroxide

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Water molecules in crystalline hydrates can be bound directly to a central metal ion (coordinated water), trapped in crystal lattice voids (interstitial water), or held by hydrogen bonds outside the coordination sphere.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
- In \([\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]^{3+} 3\mathrm{Cl}^-\), all six water molecules are directly coordinated to the \(\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}\) ion, representing coordinated water.
- \(\mathrm{BaCl}_2 \cdot 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) is a classic example of interstitial water.
- In \(\mathrm{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), written as \([\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_4]^{2+}\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}\cdot \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), the single water molecule outside the coordination sphere is hydrogen-bonded water.
- \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2 \cdot \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) is the solid hydrate formed by hydrogen peroxide with water (melting point \(221\text{ K}\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hence, \([\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]^{3+} 3\mathrm{Cl}^-\) corresponds to coordinated water, \(\mathrm{BaCl}_2 \cdot 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) to interstitial water, the outer water molecule in \(\mathrm{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) to hydrogen-bonded water, and \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2 \cdot \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) to the hydrate of hydrogen peroxide.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MATCHING_Q07 - Preparation methods of hydrogen peroxide

questiontext.text:
Match the preparation method in List I with the reactants or intermediates in List II:

List IList II
(A) Acidification of barium peroxide(i) \(\mathrm{K}_2\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_8(\mathrm{s}) + 2\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\)
(B) Electrolytic oxidation of acidified sulphate(ii) 2-Ethylanthraquinol + \(\mathrm{O}_2\) (air)
(C) Laboratory preparation of \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}_2\)(iii) \(\mathrm{BaO}_2 \cdot 8\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4(\mathrm{aq})\)
(D) Industrial auto-oxidation process(iv) Hydrolysis of \(\mathrm{HO}_3\mathrm{SOOSO}_3\mathrm{H}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hydrogen peroxide (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\)) and its deuterated analogue (\(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}_2\)) are prepared by specific chemical and electrochemical routes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
- Acidifying \(\mathrm{BaO}_2 \cdot 8\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) with \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) precipitates \(\mathrm{BaSO}_4\) and yields \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\).
- Electrolytic oxidation of acidified sulphate solutions at high current density produces peroxodisulphate (\(\mathrm{HO}_3\mathrm{SOOSO}_3\mathrm{H}\)), which on hydrolysis yields \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\).
- Laboratory preparation of \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) uses the hydrolysis of potassium peroxodisulphate (\(\mathrm{K}_2\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_8\)) with heavy water (\(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\)).
- Industrially, \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) is manufactured by the auto-oxidation of 2-alkylanthraquinols (such as 2-ethylanthraquinol) in air.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, barium peroxide acidification pairs with \(\mathrm{BaO}_2 \cdot 8\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\), electrolytic oxidation with hydrolysis of \(\mathrm{HO}_3\mathrm{SOOSO}_3\mathrm{H}\), laboratory \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) synthesis with \(\mathrm{K}_2\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_8 + 2\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\), and industrial auto-oxidation with 2-ethylanthraquinol + \(\mathrm{O}_2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MATCHING_Q08 - Electrolytic methods for dihydrogen production

questiontext.text:
Match the electrolytic process in List I with its characteristic feature in List II:

List IList II
(A) Electrolysis of acidified water(i) Warm aqueous \(\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}\) between nickel electrodes
(B) High-purity (>99.95%) \(\mathrm{H}_2\)(ii) \(\mathrm{H}^-\) oxidised to \(\mathrm{H}_2\) at the anode
(C) Electrolysis of brine solution(iii) Uses platinum electrodes with traces of acid/base
(D) Electrolysis of molten saline hydride(iv) \(\mathrm{Cl}_2\) at anode; \(\mathrm{H}_2\) and \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) formed at cathode

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Dihydrogen can be generated electrolytically from aqueous solutions or molten hydrides, with the electrode materials and half-reactions depending on the electrolyte.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
- Electrolysis of acidified water (containing traces of acid or base) uses platinum electrodes to give \(\mathrm{H}_2\) and \(\mathrm{O}_2\).
- High-purity (\(>99.95\%\)) dihydrogen is obtained by electrolysing warm aqueous barium hydroxide solution between nickel electrodes.
- Electrolysis of brine solution produces \(\mathrm{Cl}_2\) at the anode and \(\mathrm{H}_2\) along with \(\mathrm{OH}^-\) (\(\mathrm{NaOH}\)) at the cathode.
- Electrolysis of molten saline hydrides liberates \(\mathrm{H}_2\) at the anode via oxidation of \(\mathrm{H}^-\) ions (\(2\mathrm{H}^- \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2 + 2\mathrm{e}^-\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Matching each process to its feature gives: acidified water \(\rightarrow\) platinum electrodes, high-purity \(\mathrm{H}_2\) \(\rightarrow\) warm \(\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}\) with nickel electrodes, brine electrolysis \(\rightarrow\) \(\mathrm{Cl}_2\) at anode and \(\mathrm{H}_2/\mathrm{NaOH}\) at cathode, and molten saline hydride \(\rightarrow\) \(\mathrm{H}_2\) at anode.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MATCHING_Q09 - Redox reactions of hydrogen peroxide

questiontext.text:
Match the reactions of \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) in List I with its chemical role and medium in List II:

List IList II
(A) \(2\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} + 2\mathrm{H}^+ + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe}^{3+} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)(i) Reducing agent in basic medium
(B) \(2\mathrm{MnO}_4^- + 6\mathrm{H}^+ + 5\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 8\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} + 5\mathrm{O}_2\)(ii) Oxidising agent in basic medium
(C) \(\mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{4+} + 2\mathrm{OH}^-\)(iii) Oxidising agent in acidic medium
(D) \(\mathrm{I}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2 + 2\mathrm{OH}^- \rightarrow 2\mathrm{I}^- + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} + \mathrm{O}_2\)(iv) Reducing agent in acidic medium

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hydrogen peroxide acts as both an oxidising agent (oxygen reduced from \(-1\) to \(-2\)) and a reducing agent (oxygen oxidised from \(-1\) to \(0\) in \(\mathrm{O}_2\)) in both acidic and basic media.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
- In \(2\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} + 2\mathrm{H}^+ + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe}^{3+} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) is oxidised to \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) in the presence of \(\mathrm{H}^+\); thus \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) acts as an oxidising agent in acidic medium.
- In \(2\mathrm{MnO}_4^- + 6\mathrm{H}^+ + 5\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 8\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} + 5\mathrm{O}_2\), \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\) is reduced to \(\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}\) in acidic medium while \(\mathrm{O}_2\) is evolved; thus \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) acts as a reducing agent in acidic medium.
- In \(\mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{4+} + 2\mathrm{OH}^-\), \(\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}\) is oxidised to \(\mathrm{Mn}^{4+}\) with \(\mathrm{OH}^-\) formed; thus \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) acts as an oxidising agent in basic medium.
- In \(\mathrm{I}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2 + 2\mathrm{OH}^- \rightarrow 2\mathrm{I}^- + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} + \mathrm{O}_2\), \(\mathrm{I}_2\) is reduced to \(\mathrm{I}^-\) in basic medium; thus \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) acts as a reducing agent in basic medium.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
All four reactions match cleanly to their respective role and medium.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MATCHING_Q10 - Reactions of heavy water with compounds

questiontext.text:
Match the reaction of heavy water (\(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\)) in List I with the products formed in List II:

List IList II
(A) \(\mathrm{CaC}_2 + 2\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\)(i) \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\)
(B) \(\mathrm{SO}_3 + \mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\)(ii) \(3\mathrm{CD}_4 + 4\mathrm{Al(OD)_3}\)
(C) \(\mathrm{Al}_4\mathrm{C}_3 + 12\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\)(iii) \(2\mathrm{KDSO}_4 + \mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}_2\)
(D) \(\mathrm{K}_2\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_8 + 2\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\)(iv) \(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{D}_2 + \mathrm{Ca(OD)_2}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Heavy water (\(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\)) undergoes hydrolysis and exchange reactions analogous to ordinary water (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)), forming the corresponding deuterated compounds.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
- Calcium carbide reacts with \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\) to form deuterated acetylene and calcium deuteroxide: \(\mathrm{CaC}_2 + 2\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{D}_2 + \mathrm{Ca(OD)_2}\).
- Sulphur trioxide reacts with \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\) to form deuterated sulphuric acid: \(\mathrm{SO}_3 + \mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\).
- Aluminium carbide reacts with \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\) to form deuterated methane and aluminium deuteroxide: \(\mathrm{Al}_4\mathrm{C}_3 + 12\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{CD}_4 + 4\mathrm{Al(OD)_3}\).
- Potassium peroxodisulphate reacts with \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\) to form potassium deuterium sulphate and \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}_2\): \(\mathrm{K}_2\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_8 + 2\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{KDSO}_4 + \mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}_2\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Matching each reactant pair with its products gives the exact correspondence for all four deuteration reactions.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MATCHING_Q11 - Chemical reactions of water with compounds

questiontext.text:
Match the reaction involving water in List I with the correct product(s) in List II:

List IList II
(A) \(\mathrm{P}_4\mathrm{O}_{10}(\mathrm{s}) + 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\)(i) \(\mathrm{SiO}_2(\mathrm{s}) + 4\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{aq})\)
(B) \(\mathrm{SiCl}_4(\mathrm{l}) + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\)(ii) \(4\mathrm{H}^+(\mathrm{aq}) + 4\mathrm{F}^-(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g})\)
(C) \(\mathrm{N}^{3-}(\mathrm{s}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\)(iii) \(4\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_4(\mathrm{aq})\)
(D) \(2\mathrm{F}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\)(iv) \(\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g}) + 3\mathrm{OH}^-(\mathrm{aq})\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Water acts as a hydrolysing agent for covalent oxides, halides, and ionic nitrides, and as a reducing agent when oxidised to \(\mathrm{O}_2\) by fluorine.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
- \(\mathrm{P}_4\mathrm{O}_{10}\) undergoes hydrolysis to phosphoric acid: \(\mathrm{P}_4\mathrm{O}_{10} + 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow 4\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_4\).
- \(\mathrm{SiCl}_4\) undergoes hydrolysis to silicon dioxide and hydrochloric acid: \(\mathrm{SiCl}_4 + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{SiO}_2 + 4\mathrm{HCl}\).
- Nitride ion (\(\mathrm{N}^{3-}\)) is hydrolysed to ammonia and hydroxide ions: \(\mathrm{N}^{3-} + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{NH}_3 + 3\mathrm{OH}^-\).
- Fluorine oxidises water to dioxygen: \(2\mathrm{F}_2 + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow 4\mathrm{H}^+ + 4\mathrm{F}^- + \mathrm{O}_2\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Each reaction corresponds uniquely to its balanced product set.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MATCHING_Q12 - Physical properties of H2O and D2O

questiontext.text:
Match the physical property of \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) and \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\) in List I with the correct pair of values \((\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O},\, \mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O})\) in List II:

List IList II
(A) Boiling point (\(\mathrm{K}\))(i) \(276.98,\, 284.2\)
(B) Temperature of maximum density (\(\mathrm{K}\))(ii) \(78.39,\, 78.06\)
(C) Density at \(298\text{ K}\) (\(\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}\))(iii) \(373.0,\, 374.4\)
(D) Dielectric constant (\(\mathrm{C^2/N\cdot m^2}\))(iv) \(1.0000,\, 1.1059\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Due to the higher molecular mass of \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\) (\(20.0276\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)) compared to \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) (\(18.0151\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)), most physical constants such as boiling point, density, and temperature of maximum density are higher for \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\), while its dielectric constant is slightly lower.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
- Boiling point: \(373.0\text{ K}\) for \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) and \(374.4\text{ K}\) for \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\).
- Temperature of maximum density: \(276.98\text{ K}\) for \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) and \(284.2\text{ K}\) for \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\).
- Density at \(298\text{ K}\): \(1.0000\text{ g cm}^{-3}\) for \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) and \(1.1059\text{ g cm}^{-3}\) for \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\).
- Dielectric constant: \(78.39\) for \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) and \(78.06\) for \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Matching each physical property with its exact numerical pair gives the unique valid assignment.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MATCHING_Q13 - Applications of dihydrogen and hydrogen peroxide

questiontext.text:
Match the chemical application in List I with the substance or process in List II:

List IList II
(A) Manufacture of vanaspati fat(i) \(\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g}) + 2\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) \xrightarrow{\text{cobalt catalyst}} \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{OH}(\mathrm{l})\)
(B) Manufacture of methanol(ii) \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) sold as perhydrol
(C) Mild disinfectant and antiseptic(iii) Hydrogenation of polyunsaturated vegetable oils using \(\mathrm{Ni}\)
(D) Environmental (Green) Chemistry(iv) Oxidation of cyanides in industrial effluents using \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Both dihydrogen and hydrogen peroxide have major industrial, pharmaceutical, and environmental applications.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
- Vanaspati fat (ghee) and margarine are manufactured by catalytic hydrogenation of polyunsaturated vegetable oils (such as soyabean or cottonseed oil) using dihydrogen and a nickel catalyst.
- Bulk methanol is manufactured by reacting carbon monoxide with dihydrogen in the presence of a cobalt catalyst.
- As an antiseptic and mild disinfectant, \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) is sold in the market under the name perhydrol.
- In Environmental (Green) Chemistry, \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) is used for pollution control treatment of domestic and industrial effluents, including oxidation of cyanides and restoration of aerobic conditions to sewage wastes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Each application corresponds directly to its respective reagent or reaction.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MATCHING_Q14 - Reactions of dihydrogen and lithium hydride

questiontext.text:
Match the reaction in List I with its characteristic condition or product in List II:

List IList II
(A) \(\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{F}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{HF}(\mathrm{g})\)(i) Forms \(\mathrm{LiAlH}_4 + \mathrm{LiCl}\)
(B) \(\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{Pd}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})\)(ii) Occurs even in the dark
(C) \(8\mathrm{LiH} + \mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{Cl}_6\)(iii) Forms \(\mathrm{LiBH}_4\)
(D) \(2\mathrm{LiH} + \mathrm{B}_2\mathrm{H}_6\)(iv) Reduces \(\mathrm{Pd}^{2+}\) to \(\mathrm{Pd}(\mathrm{s})\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Dihydrogen reacts with halogens, metal ions, and metals, while unreactive saline hydrides such as \(\mathrm{LiH}\) serve as reagents to synthesize complex hydrides.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
- The reaction of \(\mathrm{H}_2\) with fluorine (\(\mathrm{F}_2\)) is so vigorous that it occurs even in the dark, whereas the reaction with iodine requires a catalyst.
- Dihydrogen reduces \(\mathrm{Pd}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})\) ions in aqueous solution to metallic palladium: \(\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{Pd}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow \mathrm{Pd}(\mathrm{s}) + 2\mathrm{H}^+(\mathrm{aq})\).
- Lithium hydride reacts with aluminium chloride dimer to form lithium aluminium hydride: \(8\mathrm{LiH} + \mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{Cl}_6 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{LiAlH}_4 + 6\mathrm{LiCl}\).
- Lithium hydride reacts with diborane to form lithium borohydride: \(2\mathrm{LiH} + \mathrm{B}_2\mathrm{H}_6 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{LiBH}_4\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Matching each reaction with its condition or product gives the exact pairing.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MATCHING_Q15 - Synthetic ion-exchange resins for demineralisation

questiontext.text:
Match the ion-exchange resin component or step in List I with its role in water demineralisation in List II:

List IList II
(A) Cation-exchange resin (\(\mathrm{RSO}_3\mathrm{H}\)) treated with \(\mathrm{NaCl}\)(i) Exchanges \(\mathrm{OH}^-\) for \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\), \(\mathrm{HCO}_3^-\), \(\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}\)
(B) Cation-exchange resin in \(\mathrm{H}^+\) form (\(\mathrm{RH}\))(ii) Converted to \(\mathrm{RNa}\) for softening hard water
(C) Anion-exchange resin (\(\mathrm{RNH}_3^+\cdot\mathrm{OH}^-\))(iii) Treated with dilute acid and alkali solutions respectively
(D) Regeneration of exhausted \(\mathrm{H}^+\) and \(\mathrm{OH}^-\) resin beds(iv) Releases \(\mathrm{H}^+\) ions, making water acidic

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Synthetic ion-exchange resins can either soften hard water by exchanging \(\mathrm{Na}^+\) for \(\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}/\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}\), or completely demineralise water by passing it successively through \(\mathrm{H}^+\)-form cation exchangers and \(\mathrm{OH}^-\)-form anion exchangers.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
- Treating \(\mathrm{RSO}_3\mathrm{H}\) with \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) converts it into \(\mathrm{RNa}\), which exchanges \(\mathrm{Na}^+\) ions for \(\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}\) ions in hard water.
- Passing water through a cation-exchange resin in the \(\mathrm{H}^+\) form (\(\mathrm{RH}\)) exchanges \(\mathrm{H}^+\) for \(\mathrm{Na}^+\), \(\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}\), \(\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}\), and other cations, releasing protons and making the water acidic.
- Passing the acidic effluent through an anion-exchange resin (\(\mathrm{RNH}_3^+\cdot\mathrm{OH}^-\)) exchanges \(\mathrm{OH}^-\) for anions like \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\), \(\mathrm{HCO}_3^-\), and \(\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}\); the liberated \(\mathrm{OH}^-\) ions neutralise the \(\mathrm{H}^+\) ions to form \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\).
- Exhausted cation and anion exchange resin beds are regenerated by treatment with dilute acid and dilute alkali solutions respectively.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
All four steps in synthetic resin softening and demineralisation match their exact functions.
